title: Kingdom of Rheged
capsule: Rheged was a Brittonic-speaking post-Roman kingdom of the Hen Ogledd ('Old North'), likely centered on Carlisle and covering much of modern Cumbria and Dumfries and Galloway, known almost entirely through the praise poetry of Taliesin celebrating its greatest king, Urien Rheged (fl. c. 570–590). Urien led a coalition of northern British kingdoms that besieged the Anglians on Lindisfarne before being assassinated, allegedly through the treachery of a rival British king named Morcant Bwlc. The kingdom was absorbed into Northumbria without recorded military conquest, most likely through the marriage of the Bernician prince Oswiu to the Rhegedian princess Rieinmelth around 638.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Rheged is among the most poorly attested early medieval British kingdoms; its territorial extent is speculative, reconstructed from indirect linguistic, genealogical, and poetic evidence, and cannot be mapped with any precision.
